items.summary: An estimate below -2.76 SD (the 0.04R inner clamp) or above +3 SD is now marked as off scale and is never drawn like a stub. geometry.ts: THETA_CLAMP_LOW and offScaleOf(theta) -> 'none' | 'low' | 'high'. profile.ts: SpokeEstimate.offScale, set by measuredFields. blob.ts: SpokeView.offScale + arrow (an arrowhead path whose tip is on the clamp radius, pointing towards the centre for low and out of the rim for high, 12 x 13 user units), the marker stays at the clamped radius, the whisker keeps whatever part of the range lies inside the scale, and the spoke label gets an italic 'off scale' note line like a stub gets 'not measured'. The radius map is untouched (linear in theta, clamped to [0.04R, R]). BlobChart.svelte draws the arrow instead of the dot (hollow when muted). BarTable.svelte draws an arrowhead at the track end instead of the dot, skips a range with no drawn length, and puts '(off scale)' after the estimate. copy.ts: OFF_SCALE_LABEL, OFF_SCALE_CAPTION (blob figcaption) and OFF_SCALE_BARS_NOTE (bar view), each shown only when a drawn spoke is off scale (also under a facet chart). card.ts mirrors the arrow, the note line and its italic style (card.dom.test.ts compares the card with the page chart element by element). synthetic.ts has a fifth demo profile 'offscale' (PS far below, RT above the scale) for #/dev/blob?profile=offscale. ProfileView overrides a build-up frame's off-scale mark with the final estimate's, so spokes still to be revealed (growing from -3 SD) do not flash arrows.

blob.test.ts 'estimates beyond the scale...' (fast-check, theta in [-6, 6]): theta below the clamp -> offScale 'low', marker and arrow tip on 0.04R; above +3 -> 'high' on R; in between the marker is at R(theta + 3)/6 within 0.15 px and has no arrow; a measured spoke never has a stub or gap; arrow direction; whisker keeps its inside part; 'off scale' label line
profile.test.ts: every measured estimate records offScale, a stub has none
card.test.ts: arrowheads on the card instead of dots, 'off scale' labels, marker radii match r(theta); no arrow for in-range cards
card.dom.test.ts: card and BlobChart agree element by element for a model with two off-scale spokes
ProfileView.ux.dom.test.ts: arrow, no stub, caption sentence only when needed; bar view arrow, '(off scale)' cell, bar note; far-off range not drawn as a dot

e2e/ux-viz.spec.ts (chromium, iphone, webkit): #/dev/blob?profile=offscale shows two arrows ('low' at 0.04R, 'high' at R, measured from the path), no stub, 'off scale' labels, the caption; bar view arrows and '(off scale)'; axe clean
items.notes: Wording differs slightly from the triage: the arrow sentence says 'at or past the end of the scale (-3 or +3 SD)' because an estimate between -3 and -2.76 SD is also drawn on the clamp. The note is two constants (blob view / bar view) so each says only what is on screen. The label note line makes labels one line taller for off-scale spokes (fitLayout sees them, it works from the final estimates).

items.summary: The share card is designed for a 600 px read (every text >= 20 card px = 10 px at 600 wide). card.ts: the chart's own text (spoke labels ~24 px, ring labels ~21 px, only -2/0/+2 SD labelled via the new BlobOptions.ringStep) comes from a new placeBlob that searches every collision-free layout (full or one-line labels, fonts 12.5-48) with layoutExtent, takes the first TEXT_TARGETS value (21.2, 20.5, 20, 18 ... 11) that some layout reaches and, among the layouts that reach it, the one with the largest circle; this now reaches 21 px text for 3 to 17 skills (the old fit managed 11-16 px). Column: brand 28, title 44, sessions 22, peaks heading 24, peak names 22, numbers 20. New full-width small print (footerTexts): the three caveat sentences and the purpose line as one wrapped paragraph, the key 'Filled: range clear of 0 SD. Hollow: range overlaps 0 SD.' + 'SD means standard deviation.', and the ring note ('Rings: SD units, provisional' / 'Centre: -3 SD') as its own texts at 20 px; the in-chart ring note is left out of the card's blob (BlobOptions.note = false, BlobModel.showNote, BlobChart honours it). Every existing caveat sentence is kept word for word ('Ranges that overlap are not real differences.' still appears exactly once).
tests_added: card.test.ts: no text under 20 card px (column, small print, chart text after scale) for 3..17 skills and any subset; small print runs full width, rows do not overlap, last baseline 24 px from the edge; column fits its width for three long-named peaks and ends above the small print; circle > 340 px for 5-7 skills; key sentence, SD meaning, ring note texts and the overlap sentence exactly once; the key matches the drawn hollow/filled marks; ring labels only -2, 0, +2 SD; band outline in the card stylesheet
blob.test.ts: BlobOptions.note = false drops the note from the viewBox; ringStep = 2 labels only -2/0/+2
tests_changed: card.test.ts: allowed-text check now accepts runs of the wrapped small print and the new lines; markerRadii also reads arrow tips; the palette check skips the numeric bandEdgeOpacity; the layout/frame checks use the new chart region and the 20 px floor (they asserted the old 11 px floor and the old 448 px column / 700 px chart edge)
items.notes: Deviations from the triage text: (1) the card keeps the string 'Rings: SD units, provisional' (e2e/share-card.spec.ts, reveal-owned, matches that text node exactly) and spells SD out in the key line instead of renaming it; the footnotes are one flowing paragraph rather than 'one or two lines' (the caveats do not fit in two lines at 20 px). (2) The ring ('outer ring') is about 300-400 card px across, not 440: with 24 px labels on a 704 x 472 chart region the text size wins over circle size (the old card was 316 px with 14 px text). Card circle size varies with label lengths. share-card.spec.ts passes on chromium and iphone.

items.notes: Two deviations, both because of the existing phone legibility floors: (1) PS is 'Processing' (the first word of 'Processing & Reading Speed'), not 'Reading speed': 'Reading speed' is the widest label (it sits at 9 o'clock) and took the 17-spoke chart at 288 px to 8.3 px text, and it also starts with the word 'Reading' that 'Reading comp.' uses. (2) The vertical clearance between neighbouring labels is 0.2 em of the label size, not a full line: 0.5 em already took the m1 chart at 328 px below 11 px, a full line would take it below 9 px at 288. The remaining ambiguity (labels stacked above one another) is addressed by the names, not the gap.
